previousStagingSocketRestartCheck.restartMode: Railway in-place restart of the existing deployment
previousStagingSocketRestartCheck.scope: Authorized staging-only restart during an active two-client match. Clients did not receive the restart notice and closed abnormally; the service recovered, the old reconnect token was rejected, and a new room started. Reward claiming was not tested.

latestLocalSocketSignalComparison.wrapperSignal: SIGTERM sent to the pnpm process; no client shutdown notice or WebSocket close was observed within 10 seconds
latestLocalSocketSignalComparison.interpretation: The pnpm wrapper did not close sockets locally, while direct Node did; a local gateway-plus-socket test also passed. Live results differ by harness: a two-client raw Railway probe closed both clients with 1006 and no notice, while a later one-pilot browser displayed the server-restart message. Multi-pilot delivery remains unresolved.

latestLocalGatewayShutdownCheck.scope: Local staging gateway proxy with a direct Node socket process; SIGTERM delivered the interruption notice to both clients and the proxy forwarded close code 4002. This does not establish Railway service-restart behavior.

priorStagingSocketRestartCheckBeforeShut.restartMode: Railway in-place restart after successful direct-Node start-command deployment
priorStagingSocketRestartCheckBeforeShut.scope: After an explicitly authorized staging-only start-command update and successful deployment, an active two-client match was interrupted by an in-place Railway restart. Neither client received the interruption notice; both closed with 1006. The service recovered and a fresh room started. No reward claim was attempted.

stagingSocketRestartCheckBeforeAckFix.restartMode: Authorized Railway in-place restart of the deployed staging socket
stagingSocketRestartCheckBeforeAckFix.scope: The tested socket source was deployed to staging and Railway's /healthz check passed. In the live two-pilot restart, neither client received the restart notice and both closed with 1006. The service recovered and two clients started a distinct fresh room. The stale-session assertion is not counted because the probe did not send the prior reconnect token. No reward claim was attempted; no second restart was run.

latestStagingSocketRestartCheck.restartMode: Authorized Railway in-place restart of the deployed staging socket
latestStagingSocketRestartCheck.scope: Two raw WebSocket protocol pilots entered an active staging match through the protected staging gateway and sent neutral inputs every 250 ms to remain active. After the authorized socket restart, both received server_restart, wrote acknowledgements, and closed with code 4002; Railway logged acknowledged=2 with no timeouts or send errors. The old reconnect token was rejected with session_lost, and two clients started a distinct fresh room. No Clerk sign-in, reward request, or physical-device test was performed.

latestStagingBrowserRestartCheck.scope: An approved staging account reached an active one-pilot browser match. After the staging socket restart, the UI returned to the menu and showed its server_restart no-rewards message. This proves the visible message for one browser pilot, not delivery to all pilots; an earlier two-client raw protocol run observed close code 1006 and no notice.

latestStagingBrowserFreshRoomCheck.scope: One authenticated staging browser started an online room, received the server_restart no-rewards message after the staging socket restart, then used Create New Room to generate a different room and start another match. Room codes were not recorded. This establishes the browser recovery flow for one pilot, not all-player restart notification. The online-room path does not call the separate server-authorized Strike claim API.

latestStagingAccountAndRoomUiCheck.scope: Protected staging only, using two existing approved accounts. /api/world and /api/market returned data for both accounts. A profile query carrying the other account's userId returned the authenticated caller's profile; a profile action carrying a foreign userId was rejected with HTTP 400. The first full-profile comparison differed; a repeat stability check and a second before/after comparison around the rejected write were stable. Browser room-code invite, separate team assignment, the host readiness gate, both-pilot readiness, and match start passed with three canvases per browser. No market trade, new account, reward claim, or Production change was made. This does not certify physical-device sync or world-state cross-account mutations.

latestStagingSharedMarketTradeCheck.scope: Protected staging only. Earlier codes left both contexts at needs_client_trust; the rendered challenge had one six-digit field, a visible Continue button, no visible error, and no Turnstile frame. Fresh codes for the active challenges authenticated both existing accounts and each profile returned HTTP 200. One salt was bought and sold back. The observer saw shared stock decrease and return, and the buyer's inventory/cargo returned to baseline. The buyer's balance decreased by two credits from spread/price impact; market revision advanced twice. Both accounts signed out to HTTP 401. Production was not accessed or modified.
